result.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Wheelchair Configuration Classification in Accessible Automated Vehicle Applications
result.summary: Making automated vehicles accessible requires consideration of vulnerable road users, including wheelchair users. To offer a more tailored experience that supports independence for this group, vehicle design needs to accommodate the wide range of wheelchair configurations. However, wheelchairs are individualized, varying in frame geometry, propulsion, and visual appearance. Moreover, occupants or accessories may obscure visual cues. Existing mobility-aid datasets only label the presence of a wheelchair, rather than describing its specific configuration. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), comprising 467 face-blurred images across 192 capture groups solely for evaluation. Each image is annotated with (i) a two-class label of manual or powered, (ii) a chair subtype, (iii) occupancy, viewpoint, setting, lighting, occlusion, propulsion, and control, with a 273-image validation split and 194-image test split. Three convolutional neural network backbones and a frozen vision-language probe are trained on an external image dataset and evaluated on WCID to measure cross-dataset generalization, while also testing robustness using Gaussian blur. Convolutional models do well on clean images, but performance drops under strong blur, leaving a gap before deployment. Code, split assignments, labels, trained weights, and the face-blurred images is available at: https://github.com/Mi3-Lab/MAID

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 WCID 轮椅构型图像数据集（467 张、仅用于评测，标注手动/电动、子类型、占用、视角、遮挡、光照等），并在外部数据上训练三种 CNN backbone 与一个冻结 VLM probe，考察跨数据集泛化及高斯模糊下的鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其冻结视觉语言 probe 与遮挡、模糊条件标注，可能可供核查 VLM 内部状态是否保留细粒度视觉属性及其证据筛选的脆弱性；但论文本身不涉及 latent 推理状态或停止决策，仅属外围线索，需较多核查。
